Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteración de señal difusa la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales continuos.
Rotura compleja / maceración degenerativa del menisco lateral con extrusión del remanente
meniscal, quiste parameniscal de 7 x 6 mm y edema de las partes blandas para meniscales.
Fibrilación del borde libre del menisco medial.
Cartílago femorotibial con alteración de señal, irregularidad superficial y defectos parciales,
asociado a úlceras de espesor total con cambios óseos reactivos en la superficie carga y tercio
posterior de no carga del cóndilo femoral lateral y ulcera de espesor subtotal en la superficie carga
del cóndilo femoral medial sin cambios óseos reactivos. Destaca amplio defecto condral de
espesor completo con cambios óseos reactivos en el platillo tibial lateral, mide 13 mm medio
lateral x 8 mm anteroposterior que se acompaña de quiste subcondral en el platillo tibial y gruesas
prominencias osteofíticas marginales.
Cartílago patelofemoral de espesor y señal conservados sin defectos condrales profundos.
Engrosamiento con alteración de señal y cambios entesopaticos cuadricipitales distales.
Alteración de señal del tendón rotuliano proximal y distal.
Restantes tendones regionales de espesor y señal conservados.
Moderado derrame articular con signos de sinovitis difusa.
Probable gangliones en relación la inserción femoral de ambos gastrocnemios y tendón poplíteo.
Quiste poplíteo 26 x 21 x 49 mm con signos de leve filtración.
Trofismo muscular conservado.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja / maceración degenerativa del menisco lateral con extrusión del remanente,
quiste parameniscal y edema de partes blandas para meniscales.
Fibrilación del borde libre del menisco medial.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 del compartimento femorotibial lateral. Condropatía lesiones
grado 2 y 3 del cóndilo femoral medial.
Tendinosis y entesopatía cuadricipital distal. Tendinosis rotuliana proximal y distal.
Moderado derrame articular con signos de sinovitis difusa.
Quiste poplíteo con signos de leve filtración

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Lesión meniscal versus condral lateral izquierda.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Aumento de señal central del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del menisco medial de
predominio periférico, sugiriendo una rotura, no desplazada.
El menisco lateral impresiona presentar una rotura vertical periférica de su cuerno posterior, sin
desplazamiento de segmentos.
Cartílagos los compartimentos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Aumento de señal del aspecto superoexterno de la grasa de Hoffa.
No hay evidente derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano con roturas parciales
de las fibras profundas y centrales que mide aproximadamente 7 x 6 mm en sus ejes mayores,
con extensión hacia cefálico por la aponeurosis prepatelar con cambios óseos reparativos
regionales.
Leve aumento de sedación distal del tendón cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura.
Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Signos de una rotura periférica del menisco medial, no desplazada.
Rotura vertical periférica del cuerno posterior del menisco lateral, no desplazada.
Discretos signos de un síndrome de hiperpresión externa de rótula.
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal con rotura parcial y extensión hacia la aponeurosis prepatelar con
cambios óseos reparativos regionales.
Leve tendinosis cuadricipital dista

MRI  KNEE  -  RIGHT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Progressive right knee pain. Prior external ultrasound report details "unexplained knee joint effusion, recommend further evaluation with MRI to assess this sclerotic distal femoral lesion and for any possible internal derangement".

COMPARISON:  No prior imaging

FINDINGS:

Medial meniscus:  Intact.

Medial compartment articular cartilage:  Severe thinning of the articular cartilage of the medial tibiofemoral joint.

MCL:  Intact.

Lateral meniscus:  Intact.

Lateral compartment articular cartilage:  Mild thinning of the cartilage of the lateral tibiofemoral joint. There is slight concavity and cartilaginous thinning along the weightbearing aspect of the lateral femur, may be in keeping with an old osteochondral injury.

LCL complex:  Intact.

ACL:  Intact.

PCL:  Intact.

Quadriceps and patellar tendons:  Intact.

Patellofemoral alignment:  Normal 

Patellofemoral cartilage:  Severe chondrosis of the medial trochlea. Moderate cartilage thinning of the patella. No bony edema.

Joint effusion:  Small

Intra-articular bodies:  None.

Bone marrow:  Normal.

Popliteal fossa:  Normal.

Other findings:  Partially imaged distal femur. There is a T1 hypointense possibly expansile lesion partially visualized.


INTERPRETATION:

Mild-to-moderate degenerative changes of the medial compartment. Moderate to severe degenerative changes of the patellofemoral compartment.

The femur is not completely visualized on this knee MRI. There is a distal femur lesion, minimally visualized. Dedicated CT or MRI of the femur are recommended to further characterize this lesion.

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  There is complete rupture of the posterolateral bundle of ACL. The anteromedial bundle is structurally continuous. Normal PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is minor fraying of the lateral compartment articular cartilage. Normal medial compartment articular cartilage. Minor focal edema is noted within the lateral patellar facet articular cartilage. Normal trochlear articular cartilage.  
Conclusion: Ruptured posterolateral bundle of ACL. Minor fraying of the lateral compartment articular cartilage. No lateral meniscal tear.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Left knee pain.

COMPARISON:  Correlated with knee radiograph dated [Date].

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

There is a tear involving the posterior root of the medial meniscus, characterized by disruption at its root attachment adjacent to the tibial plateau.

Extensive intrasubstance degeneration of the anterior and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. No evidence of discrete tear.

ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL are intact.

Scattered area of chondrosis cartilaginous irregularities more prominent at the patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment.

Small volume joint effusion.

Benign cystic changes at the tibial spine/tibial eminence.

The extensor mechanism is intact, the quadriceps tendon and patellar tendon are unremarkable.

No bone marrow edema.

2.6 x 2.5 x 6.7 cm Baker's cyst.


INTERPRETATION:

Posterior root tear of the medial meniscus.

Extensive intrasubstance degeneration of the lateral meniscus without evidence of tear.

Scattered area of chondrosis with no evidence of fissuring or full thickness cartilage loss. Findings in keeping with mild OA.

Incidental finding of 6.7 cm Baker's cyst.

EXAM TYPE: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
EXAM DATE AND TIME: [DATE] [TIME]
INDICATION: [IDENTIFIER]
COMPARISON: None

Impression:  

1. Fracture involving the posterior and anterior horns of the medial meniscus.

2. Microtrabecular insufficiency fracture involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle and probably the medial tibial plateau, with surrounding marrow edema as well as medial compartment osteoarthritis.

3. Marrow contusions involving the anterior aspect of the medial and lateral tibial plateau.


Technique:  Magnetic Resonance Imaging of the right knee was performed utilizing sagittal T2 weighted and fat suppressed proton density, coronal T1 weighted and fat suppressed proton density, and axial fat suppressed T2 weighted sequences.


Comment:

Menisci: The lateral meniscus is intact. There is a complex fracture involving the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with extrusion of the meniscal body. There is also a horizontal fracture involving the anterior horn of the medial meniscus.

Cruciate ligaments: Intact

Collateral ligaments: Intact

Extensor mechanism: Quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Joint fluid/Baker's cyst: There is a small to moderate joint effusion. There is also a moderate complex Baker's cyst which appears partially ruptured.

Bone marrow: A small crescentic focus of signal abnormality is noted in the subchondral weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle, compatible with a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture with surrounding marrow edema. There is slight flattening of the articular surface at the site of the fracture. An additional small microtrabecular insufficiency fracture is suspected in the medial tibial plateau. There is also marrow edema along the anterior aspect of the medial and lateral tibial plateau suggesting marrow contusions.

Femorotibial joints: There is cartilage thinning involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial compartment, with joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation compatible with osteoarthritis. Mild cartilage thinning and heterogeneity are noted in the weightbearing aspect of the lateral compartment.

Patellofemoral joint: There is mild cartilage heterogeneity along the posterior patella.

MRI of right Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc RT, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Ax DWI B800, Screen Save



> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst about 8 cm in length.
> Small size and linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> No strong MR evidence of tear of lateral meniscus.
> Osteoarthritis of right knee joint with spur formation and subchondral bone marrow edema/cysts ( major in femoral condyle) and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage, more severe at medial compartment.
  Grade 3-4 chondromalacia of medial patella
> Interstitial increased signal of ACL on F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury of degeneration.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
  Frond-like depositions of fatty tissue in the suprapatellar bursa, R/O lipoma arborescens (diffuse synovial lipoma)
> PCL and medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Subcutaneous edmea over right knee.
> Some varicose veins.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee, more prominent at medial compartment with grade 4 chondromalacia.
2. Synovitis of right knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae; R/O Lipoma arborescens.
3. Baker's cyst with perifocal edmea.
4. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
5. Subcutaneous edmea over right knee and some varicose veins.
6. Grade 1 injury of ACL. 
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Findings:  There is a minor knee effusion. There is an undisplaced complex tear of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Normal lateral meniscus.  ACL is mildly attenuated suggesting a previous partial sprain. Normal PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Focal moderate patellar ridge and medial patellar facet articular cartilage thinning is noted with associated underlying bony change. Normal tibiofemoral and trochlear articular cartilage. Normal visualized bones and surrounding soft tissues.  
Conclusion: Minor effusion. Undisplaced tear of the posteromedial corner of the medial meniscus. Suspected old partial ACL injury. Patellar chondropathy noted.
